newsitem.title: USA: Stocks up on triple witching; bonds, dollar firmer.
newsitem.headline: Stocks up on triple witching; bonds, dollar firmer.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks rose Friday, while the S&P 500 closed at a record high as the market was boosted by triple-witching futures and options expirations.
Bonds edged higher and the dollar rose moderately before the Federal Reserve's policy-setting meeting on Tuesday.
The Dow Jones industrial average closed 20.72 points higher at 5,888.46, just shy of Monday's all-time high finish of 5,889.20, after hitting 5,897 earlier. For the week, the Dow rose 49.94 points.
"We had some good strength on blue chips and Nasdaq and a hint of profit-taking as the day came to a close," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.

In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,414 to 902 on very heavy volume of 514 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange, swollen by the expiration of September futures and options.
It was the most active NYSE session since July 16's record 680 million shares.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks rose 4.02 to 687.02, topping Monday's record close of 683.98. The index was up 6.48 on the week.

Wall Street will be waiting for Tuesday's meeting of the Federal Reserve's policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee. Many Wall Street analysts expect a modest increase in short-term interest rates to head off inflationary pressures.
In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury bond edged up 1/32, reducing its yield to 7.04 percent from 7.05 percent at Thursday's close.
In late New York trading, the dollar stood at 1.5160 marks late Friday, up from 1.5136 marks late Thursday. The dollar traded at 109.96 Japanese yen, up from 109.44 yen.

At the Commodity Exchange, December gold ended down $1.70 at $383.90 an ounce after falling to a three-year low earlier at $383.30, as the outlook for mild inflation reduced the demand for precious metals.
December silver ended down 7.7 cents at $4.863 per ounce, after hitting three-year low earlier at $4.840.
At the New York Mercantile Exchange, crude oil for October delivery expired 9 cents higher at $23.63 a barrel, but went off the board well below last Friday's settlement of $24.51 a barrel.

Overseas, London's FTSE rose as high as 3,994.1 points but slid to end the week at 3,964.1 points, down 10.2 points on the day, for a fall of 3.8 since last week. In Tokyo, the key 225-issue Nikkei average closed down 210.61 points at 21,112.24, up 269.6 from a week ago.
